keyFindings.description: `bun run typecheck` in packages/pi-legion fails: TurnState's `options: Required<AskOption>[]` now requires the `id` this PR adds to AskOption, so seed.ts:384 and seed.test.ts:687 do not typecheck (TS2322, TS2769). CI's pi-legion job failed on exactly this at 1b191490, and ci-ok with it. Fix: type the seed's options as `Required<Omit<AskOption, "id">>` (or `Pick<AskOption, "label" | "description">` made required), since a seeded open ask carries no part id.

`bun run typecheck` in packages/claude-envoy fails on envoy-client's `{ ...edge, block: undefined }` (TS2375, TS2379), because claude-envoy compiles envoy-client under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`. CI's claude-envoy job failed on this at 1b191490. Fix: drop the key (`const { block: _held, ...rest } = edge`) instead of setting it to undefined.

The fix changed the reply rule (reply_to + reply_to_block names a block of that comment, even in an ask's thread; only ask_id names an ask part), but five published texts still give the old rule: the route description GET /api/v1 serves (this line), CreateCommentInput.reply_to_block in contracts/src/dispatch-api.ts:2872-2876, Comment.reply_block and ReplyBlock.node (dispatch-api.ts:1326, :1331, which name only a comment block), packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/AGENTS.md:640 (which still says reply_to_block in an ask's thread is 400), and the envoy changelog fragment pr2546-ask-parts.yaml. The previous round's thread asked for the first two. A client that follows them sends reply_to=<comment in the thread> to mean the ask's option and has the reply stored against the comment's block.
